The strategy of fault classification protection based on microcomputer protection and the method of residual current protection coordination based on flexible grounding are proposed. The effectiveness of the design method is proved by practical system test.

articleTitle: Joint Estimation of Terminal Voltage and Temperature in Lithium-ion Batteries for Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Accurate estimation of lithium-ion battery terminal voltage and temperature is critical to the safe operation of lithiumion batteries. Existing Li-ion battery models cannot consider both accuracy and timeliness. Taking a 280Ah square lithium-ion battery for energy storage as the research object, the article first establishes the thermal circuit-circuit coupling model of the lithium-ion battery; then, according to the experimental data of Hybrid Pulse Power Characterization (HPPC), the least squares algorithm is used to complete the parameter identification of the model. Finally, the model is validated with the experimental data. The results show that the model established in this paper considers both accuracy and timeliness.

Author Keywords: square lithium-ion battery for energy storage

articleTitle: Fast Transient Voltage Stability Assessment for Complex Receiving-End Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The continuous increase of new energy generation and AC-DC interconnection make the transient voltage stability of the receiving-end power grid more and more complicated. In order to realize the rapid assessment of transient voltage stability, a one-dimensional Convolutional Neutral Network (CNN) for transient voltage stability assessment (TVSA) is constructed by selecting the features reasonably on the basis of using the Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering (AHC) algorithm to partition the receiving-end grid. In order to enhance the assessment work, the Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) algorithm is utilized to find out the concerns of the model to features, and the model knowledge of the neural network is analyzed on the basis of surveying on a large number of samples. Based on the transient voltage stability mechanism and the concerns of deep learning model, the factors that cause transient voltage instability are analyzed. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated by the case study of a provincial grid in eastern China.

articleTitle: Design of Priority Driving Scheme for Nuclear Power Plant Protection System Based on DCS Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: CIM (Component Interface Module) is an important part of nuclear power plant protection system. Its main function is to drive the safety level actuator action after prioritizing automatic or manual commands from different safety levels, so as to complete specific safety functions. Through in-depth research on the overall architecture of DCS (Digital Control System) of ACPR1000 nuclear power unit and the transmission path of safety-level actuator drive instructions in DCS architecture, the defects of safety-level actuator controlled by NC-VDU(Non-Classified Visual Display Unit) call screen mode in existing design are summarized, and the design idea of using NC-VDU to directly control safety-level actuator is proposed. Based on the design idea, the priority driver scheme of CIM is designed. This design simplifies the operator monitoring means and the equipment size of the MCR (Main Control Room), while significantly reducing the cost, and provides a reference for the design of the compact layout of the MCR.

articleTitle: High Stability Output Current Control Method of Current Source
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of accuracy and stability of power type programmed high stable current source, this paper presents a high stable current source and its control method. Firstly, the main circuit topology and its component selection of current supply are introduced, which consists of high frequency isolated rectifier and H-bridge inverter. Secondly, the output current closed-loop and virtual impedance control strategy are adopted, combined with current command temperature drift correction technology. The current command increases as the ambient temperature increases to compensate for the temperature drift of the acquisition circuit, which can increase the stability of the current source over the full temperature range by more than 5 times. Finally, the correctness of the topology and component selection of the high stability power supply and the feasibility of the control method are verified by simulation and experiment, which has good application value.

articleTitle: Aggregation Equivalence Method for New Energy Stations Based on PSASP Modelling Loss Consistency
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Once a significant number of new energy sources have been connected, the operational characteristics of the system undergo a substantial transformation. The establishment of an equivalent model for the integration of new energy sources represents a crucial step in the assessment of the safety and stability of the power grid. The use of a detailed model for the purposes of carrying out a simulation analysis is both time-consuming and computationally intensive. It is therefore necessary to implement a reasonable equivalent simplification. This paper puts forth a novel approach to modelling the aggregation of energy stations, one that is based on the principle of loss consistency within the PSASP framework. The initial step is to construct a comprehensive model of the new energy station within the PSASP program. Subsequently, the unit response characteristics are processed in groups according to the differences in characteristics, and the equivalent impedance of the transformer and collector circuit of each group is calculated based on the principle of loss consistency. The results of the calculation example demonstrate that the aggregated equivalent model exhibits a minimal discrepancy in the dynamic response of active and reactive power under diverse fault ride-through operational scenarios. The proposed method of modelling the aggregated equivalent of new energy stations demonstrates excellent adaptability and high accuracy in the analysis of grid operation modes.

articleTitle: Construction and Application of a Power Safety Incident Evaluation System Based on the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP)
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Power safety production not only affects the safe and stable operation of the power grid but also relates to the stability of national energy supply and the reliability of electricity for the general public. However, there is currently limited research on power safety evaluation. To address this issue, this paper explores the influence of multiple factors on power safety incident evaluation and constructs a power safety incident evaluation model. First, nine evaluation indicators were identified from three dimensions: incident reporting, impact consequences and handling, and incident investigation, which serve as parameters for the power safety incident evaluation model. Next, the impact of each evaluation indicator on the power safety incident evaluation system was analyzed using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). Subsequently, each indicator was quantified, and their weights were determined to achieve power safety incident evaluation. The system was then applied to evaluate three incidents that occurred this year: the burnout of a main transformer, the burnout of a current transformer, and the burnout of a high-voltage reactor. By comparing the weighted scores of these incidents, the results demonstrated that the evaluation system could effectively assess power safety incidents.

articleTitle: Negative Valley Soft Switching Design of Three-phase Interleaved Parallel DC/DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Conventional three-phase interleaved parallel DC/DC converter systems operating at high frequency conditions increase switching losses, resulting in lower system efficiency. For this reason, this paper proposes a negative-valley inductor current soft-switching technique for DC/DC converters, which replaces the conduction loss with a smaller turn-off loss, thus improving the system efficiency. In the paper, the working principle of Buck circuit is analysed in detail, the relationship between the output current ripple and duty cycle of the interleaved Buck converter is deduced, and the general boundary conditions of inductor current for soft-switching operation are obtained by solving the KCL and KVL equations in columns, so as to derive the feasible region for soft-switching. Meanwhile, a capacitor is connected in parallel on the drain-source pole of the MOSFET to further reduce the turn-off loss. Finally, a three-phase interleaved parallel Buck converter circuit simulation model and an experimental prototype are constructed to verify the effectiveness of the technical approach, and the efficiency is as high as 97% at 4kW, which is 2.2% higher than that of the conventional three-phase interleaved parallel Buck converter.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Optimization of the OLTC: Impact on the Contamination of the Dielectric Oil in the TP01 60/22 kV Transformer of the S.E Ingenio Huancavelica
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The present research work focused on addressing the excess of on-load switch (OLTC) maneuvers in the TP01 Transformer of the Ingenio Huancavelica Substation from 2021 to 2023. This research used a quantitative, applied-type, quasi-experimental design approach, where one or more independent variables are manipulated to analyze the consequences on the dependent variable, pretest/posttest with a single group. The method used is an empirical method that is based on the knowledge and insight of the researcher. The results showed the reduction from 20 to 4 maneuvers per day, complying with the standards of the Technical Standard for the Quality of Electrical Services (NTCSE) of Peru. In addition, the level of dielectric oil contamination was mitigated from 15,742 ppm in August 2021 to 3,466 ppm in August 2023. In conclusion, the proper regulation of the Tapcon 230 Mr optimizes the control in the TP01 Transformer at the S.E. Ingenio, reducing daily maneuvers, improving operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control Based on Constrained Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization for Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In the dynamic wireless power transfer (DWPT) system for electric motor vehicles, it is certain that a reduction in coupling coefficient will reduce the system power as a result of the action of energy receiving inductor coil. And the change rate of coupling coefficient increases with the rise in vehicle speed. The model predictive control (MPC) system, when introduced, is adept at delivering precise regulation and ensuring the DWPT system's stability, even in the face of swift fluctuations in the coupling coefficient. We establish a piecewise affine (PWA) model for DC/DC converter in the DWPT system and propose multiple MPCs according to different affine intervals. In addition, we present a MPC with multi-step compensation to work normally under the delay system. For a quadratic programming (QP) problem converted from MPC, we suggest constrained adaptive particle swarm optimization (CAPSO)[1] to enhance the manipulated variable. The simulation outcomes confirm the efficacy and superiority of the suggested approach within the DWPT system.

articleTitle: Research on Battery Safety Evaluation System of Energy Storage Power Station Based on Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In the new power system, the energy storage station using lithium ion battery plays an important role in the peak and frequency modulation on the grid side, or in suppressing the power fluctuation of the new energy station on the power generation side. However, how to apply the appropriate evaluation index system to evaluate the safety risk of the battery in the operation stage is becoming more and more important. This paper first build a multi-source information fusion safety assessment system, the level of indicators including energy storage battery, battery aging degree, power condition, battery operating status, grid structure, and then based on the fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method for energy storage power station battery safety risk assessment, and gives the current risk level evaluation score. Through the calculation case of an electrochemical energy storage power station in Guangdong Province, China, according to the field information data of the energy storage power station, the actual operation state is judged to be “normal”, which is consistent with the evaluation results of this model, and proves the feasibility and accuracy of this evaluation model.

articleTitle: A Constant Power Loads Voltage Controller Based on the Coordination of Learning and Feedback Linearization
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Feedback linearization controllers are widely used in buck converters to regulate the voltage of a power system integrated by a constant power load (CPL). However, traditional feedback linearization controllers have two drawbacks. First, feedback linearization controllers are usually designed based on an approximate model of the buck converter rather than a detailed model. Second, feedback linearization controllers are practically model-based. When the parameters in the buck converter are mismatched, the performance of the feedback linearized controller deteriorates. To deal with the problems of model approximation and parameter mismatch, a reinforcement learning compensated feedback linearization (RL-FL) controller is proposed in this paper. The proposed RL-FL controller utilizes a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) to compensate the control actions obtained by the feedback linearization (FL) controller to improve the performance of voltage regulation. Subsequently, a case study is examined to verify the performance enhancement of the proposed RL-FL controller compared to the FL controller.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Scheme for New Energy Planning in a Hydropower Plant Area Based on an Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The development of a certain scale of wind and photovoltaic energy based on hydropower station has an important practical significance for realizing the scale development of renewable energy in the region of hydropower station. In this paper, a mathematical model based on the new energy planning site and investment parameters in the hydropower station area is established, with the goal of minimizing the initial investment cost of the program. The improved sparrow search algorithm is used to solve the problem, with helping to jump out of the local optimal solution. A certain hydroelectric power station area is taken as an example, this hydropower station and wind and photovoltaic energy data are obtained and analyzed, and the planning scheme combined wind, photovoltaic and hydropower to minimize the investment cost is proposed.

articleTitle: A Short Term Wind-Photovoltaic-Load Forecasting Model Based on Coupling Relationship and Multi-Layer Extraction Multi-Task Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The integration of renewable energy into the grid has deepened the uncertainty of the power system and brought difficulties to the economic dispatch of the power system. A better response is to accurately predict the Wind power, Photovoltaic power and Load power, which can provide effective data support for the economic dispatch of the power system. To this end, we propose a short-term forecast method for Wind, Photovoltaic and Load based on coupling feature mining and Multi Task Learning (MTL). Firstly, analyze and extract the correlation between the three predicted objects, and then use a Multi Layers Extraction MTL neural network as the forecast algorithm to further represent the coupling relationship between the predicted objects; Finally, a set of Wind, Photovoltaic and Load data was used as experimental data to compare and analyze the predicted results.

articleTitle: Optimization of CRM Totem Pole PFC Based on Inductor Current Zero-Crossing Prediction Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The totem-pole bridgeless PFC circuit based on GaN devices is currently a research hotspot. To achieve full-range ZVS (Zero Voltage Switching), it is necessary to select a reasonable ZCD (Zero Current Detection) sampling scheme and dead time for the inductor current in CRM (Critical Conduction Mode). Addressing the issues of large computational burden and poor reliability in current inductor current zero-crossing prediction strategies, this paper proposes optimizing the turn-off time of the freewheeling diode and the adaptive dead time to improve the reliability of inductor current zero-crossing prediction and the realization of full-range ZVS. Finally, leveraging the powerful computational capability of a high-performance DSP, the proposed method was validated through reasonable software design and the establishment of an experimental platform.

articleTitle: A Combined Methodology of a Finite Element Method and a Sine Cosine Optimization Algorithm for Inversions of the Thermal Conductivity of Soil Around the High-voltage Cable Horizontal Pipe Jacking
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Horizontal pipe jacking is an important non-excavation laying way for high-voltage cable lines to cross rivers and streets. The buried depth of horizontal pipe jacking is generally deep, and most of the heat generated in the cable is dissipated through the soil surrounding the pipe. However, the surrounding soil texture and water content distribution are complex for different regions and seasons, resulting in a significant variation in the corresponding soil thermal conductivity. Moreover, it is impossible to directly measure the soil thermal conductivity in engineering applications. In this point of view, a numerical model for numerical calculations of the coupled thermal-fluid field under the horizontal pipe jacking laying of a dual-circuit high-voltage cable is first developed, and the equivalent thermal conductivity is inversed using a standardized improved sine cosine optimization algorithm to obtain the soil thermal conductivity under the practical laying condition, and finally used to calculate the cable current ratting under this laying way. The standardized improvement of the sine cosine algorithm enhances its search ability and its solution speed.

Author Keywords: Horizontal pipe jacking for high-voltage power cable

articleTitle: EV Charging Load Forecasting Method Considering Time-of-Use Price and Meteorological Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The randomness of load fluctuations at electric vehicle (EV) charging stations presents a significant challenge for the accurate load forecasting. Considering time-of-use (TOU) price and meteorological factors, EV charging load forecasting method for EV charging station is proposed. First, the factors affecting charging load are analyzed using the Pearson correlation coefficient and the maximum information coefficient (MIC). Key factors such as TOU price, temperature, weekday type, and recent historical load data are determined. Next, convolutional neural network (CNN) is used to extract important features and capture complex nonlinear relationships from key factors. Finally, the extracted features are processed by gated recurrent unit (GRU) network to forecast charging load at different time scales. Case study is conducted using load data from EV charging station with a capacity of 1800 kW. The results demonstrate that the CNN-GRU model significantly improves forecasting accuracy at 4h, 24h, 72h, and 168h forecasting lengths compared to other models.

articleTitle: Admittance Modeling and Application of AC-Side Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of distributed energy resources, the electrification trend of power systems through power electronics is evident. However, when converters are interconnected with the grid, local grid instability may occur. To address the issue of local instability question, this paper develops an input admittance model for converters that accounts for DC-side voltage fluctuations. By analyzing the impact of current inner loop bandwidth and phase-locked loop(PLL) bandwidth on input admittance, and using the generalized Nyquist stability criterion to study system stability, the accuracy of the model and the correctness of the stability criterion are verified with simulation results. This provides a theoretical basis for designing more stable converter parameters. By comparing models that consider and do not consider DC-side voltage fluctuations, it is found that the former is more accurate. The influence of controller parameters on the admittance model is studied, and the system stability is analyzed using the generalized Nyquist stability criterion, providing a reference for converter parameter design.

articleTitle: Novel Discontinuous Modulation Strategy for Z-Source Inverters Using Equal Time Interval Shoot-Through State Insertion Method
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The conventional Z-source inverter shoot-through vector insertion method usually inserts a shoot-through vector between two different voltage vectors, which does not additionally increase the number of switching actions. However, the variation of the voltage vector dwell time will cause the fluctuation of the inductor ripple. In this paper, a modulation strategy with an equal time interval shoot-through vector insertion method is proposed. By utilizing the discontinuous modulation strategy and selecting lower switching loss shoot-through vectors, the reduction of inductor ripple is achieved with essentially no increase in losses. The effectiveness of the proposed modulation strategy is demonstrated by MATLAB/Simulink combined with PLECS simulation.

articleTitle: A Complete Condition Monitoring Method for SiC MOSFETs with BTI Recovery Function
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Real-time condition monitoring (CM) of various degradation modes is an effective way to improve reliability of Silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs. Currently, gate-oxide and bond wire degradation are the focus of attention. However, it is a challenge to monitor these two degradation modes independently. In this article, a complete degradation monitoring method for SiC MOSFETs based on short-circuit (SC) conditions is proposed, which can separate different degradation modes and has BTI recovery function. By triggering one cycle of SC condition, the gate-oxide degradation can be monitored by detecting the peak value of SC current. Then, the voltage ringing between Kelvin source and power source <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(v_{\mathrm{K}\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}})$</tex> can reflect bond wire degradation. In order to decouple the effect of gate-oxide degradation, the voltage ringing of the circuit parasitic inductance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(v_{\text{EQU}})$</tex> is introduced, and the ratio of their peak values is taken as bond wire degradation precursor. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through experiments.

articleTitle: The Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Prediction Model Based on FCM-BLS
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In recent years, the application of deep learning in photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting has demonstrated high prediction accuracy, but it is also accompanied by limitations such as long training times. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel short-term PV power prediction model based on Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) and the Broad Learning System (BLS). First, a self-organizing map is employed to finely cluster PV power data at different time points, extracting power fluctuation characteristics under various meteorological conditions. Then, a multi-step prediction model based on BLS is constructed. By expanding the number of nodes along the network's width and training the neural network through the pseudo-inverse of matrices, the model achieves a strong capability for high-dimensional data fitting while enhancing computational efficiency. Finally, simulation analyses are conducted using real-world PV power data, and the proposed model is compared with conventional forecasting methods, demonstrating its significant advantages in both prediction accuracy and training efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on Power of Damped AC Voltage While Conducting Simultaneous Three-Phase Partial Discharge Test on 10kV Distribution Cable
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The 10 kV distribution cable is extensively used in urban power grids; however, minor defects introduced during the production, construction, and operational phases can lead to partial discharges within these cables. Such discharges significantly compromise the safe and stable operation of the distribution system. Currently, damped AC voltage technology is widely used on-site to detect and locate partial discharge defects in 10 kV distribution cables. With the growing demand for improved efficiency in operation and maintenance, researchers have begun to explore the simultaneous detection of partial discharges across all three phases of distribution cables using damped AC voltage testing systems. The power demand characteristics required for simultaneously detecting three phases are influenced by various factors such as load capacity, insulation resistance, and more. Therefore, this paper analyzes the power characteristics required for simultaneous damped AC voltage testing of three-phase 10 kV distribution cables through simulation. Initially, the working principle of DC charging damped AC voltage is introduced. Subsequently, a Simulink simulation model is constructed based on this principle. The simulation encompasses various scenarios, including single-phase testing, three-phase simultaneous testing, and three-phase simultaneous testing with reduced insulation resistance due to defects. The analysis yields critical data, such as the charging voltage applied to the tested cable, the damped AC voltage waveform, and the charging current from the power supply. Additionally, the study calculates the required boosting time and the power demand characteristics for the three-phase simultaneous test under these conditions, as well as the energy consumed during these scenarios.

articleTitle: Fault Section Location Method for Resonant Grounding System Based on MVMD-TKEO Combined with Time Difference
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: With the increasing complexity and operational requirements of power systems, the problem of fault location in resonant grounding systems has become increasingly important. This paper proposes a fault section location method based on multivariate variational mode decomposition (MVMD) combined with Teager Kaiser Energy Operator (TKEO) and time difference. Specifically, firstly, the line mode component of the fault three-phase voltage signal is extracted through phase mode transformation, and the highest frequency feature signal is extracted using the MVMD method to reduce noise interference and preserve critical fault information. Then, perform the TKEO operation on the highest frequency intrinsic modal component to obtain the arrival time of the fault wavefront, calculate the time difference, and finally use the fault time difference and the reference time difference to construct a criterion for fault section location. In a 10kV resonant grounding system, different types of fault conditions were tested, and simulation results showed that this method has good adaptability in complex power systems, providing a reliable solution for rapid fault location in resonant grounding systems.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Allocation of Operational Efficiency of Muti-Shared Energy Storages in the Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: With the introduction of the dual-carbon target, the construction of a new power system mainly based on new energy is progressing gradually, and multiple shared energy storage(SES) will be built in distribution stations to address the adequacy and flexibility caused by a high proportion of new energy. To realize the efficient call-up of multiple SES, attention needs to be paid to the comprehensive contribution of each SES to the distribution substation area. In this paper, we propose a model for evaluating and allocating the operating efficiencies of multi-SES in a station area, which takes into account the impacts of SES operation on the economy, reliability, and environment of the station area, reasonably evaluates the comprehensive operating efficiencies, and realizes the allocation of the operating efficiencies of each SES in the station area based on the Shapley model. The results show that the proposed method can effectively quantify and allocate the comprehensive performance of different SES and promote the efficient utilization of SES.

articleTitle: Development and Pilot Application of Intelligent Analyzer for Residential Electricity Consumption Situation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: With the continuous improvement of residents' living standards, the types of household appliances and electricity consumption continue to grow and the demand for household electricity consumption continues to rise. Users perceive a significant increase in electricity bills and even question the abnormal electricity prices of power supply companies which may lead to complaints or public opinion. Based on this, Jiangsu Company in line with the service tenet of “People's Power Industry for the People”, sorted out the demands of 95598 customers and combined with on-site surveys, actively analyzed the power consumption composition of customers' household appliances and independently developed the “Residential Electricity Intelligent Analyzer” operating tooling, forming an “integrated calibration, diagnosis and diagnosis” customer service plan that integrates multiple service processes such as verification, calibration and diagnosis, deeply refined the service granularity and greatly improved the level of on-site quality service.

articleTitle: Study on the Effect of Mixing Carcassone on the Performance of Composite Insulators
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In high temperature and high humidity areas, algae attach to the surface of insulation equipment as living organisms. Under long-term operation of the power grid, algae naturally age in coordination with the surface of silicone rubber, affecting the hydrophobicity of the silicone rubber surface and thus affecting the flashover voltage, posing a hidden danger to the safe and stable operation of the power system. Using Chlorella vulgaris as a representative green algae, silicone rubber materials were prepared by mixing different concentrations of Carcassone algae suppressant. The microscopic morphology of the silicone rubber samples was observed, and the surface hydrophobicity of the samples was measured. The comprehensive performance of the silicone rubber samples was analyzed and studied. The experimental results show that the best effect is achieved when the Carcassone mixing concentration is 2.0wt%, which can meet the insulation material preparation standard DL/T 376–2019 in the power industry.

articleTitle: Electrical Impedance Tomography Image Reconstruction Based on Graph Laplacian and Sparse Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) is a non-invasive diagnostic technique capable of inferring the internal conductivity distribution of a target from the measured boundary voltage signal. However, estimating high-resolution conductivity images from undersampled voltage signals is a nontrivial task due to the highly ill-posed nature of the problem. Although supervised learning methods can greatly improve the accuracy of reconstructed conductivity images, such models rely on a large number of training samples, which are difficult to obtain in practice. To address this problem, sparse regression frameworks have been introduced in EIT within the unsupervised learning setting, based on the assumption of a smaller number of inclusions. In this work, we proposed an iterative learning approach, which simultaneously incorporates spatially sparse and graph priors. Experiments conducted on both synthetic and real-world data demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analytical Model of Frequency Response of Pump Turbine of Pumped Storage Unit with Constant Speed
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In recent years, pumped storage power stations have been developing rapidly, whose importance in maintaining the frequency safety of power grids has become increasingly prominent. The water pump turbine, as an important part of the pumped storage unit, participates in the frequency response of the working process in which the parameters will change dynamically with the change of working conditions. Therefore, in this study, a method of establishing a dynamic analytical model of the frequency response is considered, reflecting the influence of external parameter changes on the frequency response characteristics of water pump turbine more obviously.

articleTitle: Research on Power System Situational Awareness under Wind Power Scale Access
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: With the increasing application range of new energy power generation, the uncertainty of distributed power generation leads to a decline in the safety of distribution network operation. New energy generation has become a trend, so it is urgent to solve the problem. The situational awareness of active distribution network becomes particularly important. In this paper, model driven method and machine learning method are used to conduct situational awareness of power grid. Two simulation methods are used in the same scene. Scenario 1 focuses on the randomness of distributed power sources. The model driven method is simulated by MATLAB, and the voltage margin overlimit index and branch overload severity index are used to evaluate the safety state of the system. The long short-term memory model was selected in the machine learning method, and the simulation was carried out in Python language in Spyder. RMSE, MAE, MAPE, Willmott's consistency index and NASH-Sutcliffe coefficient were used to evaluate the prediction accuracy of the model. Finally, the simulation results are summarized and analyzed.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Electrical Main Equipment Status Detection Based on Non-Contact Ultrasonic Measurement Principle
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Electrical equipment is an important component of the power system, and its status detection and monitoring have become key links in ensuring stable system operation and preventing accidents. Under the long-term action of alternating electromagnetic fields, power equipment will generate acoustic signals, and the changes in acoustic signals of abnormal electrical equipment can reflect the internal operating status of the equipment, as well as specific defects or faults. Non contact ultrasonic measurement technology has a wide range of application prospects in the state detection of electrical main equipment due to its non-contact, non-destructive, and safe and harmless characteristics. In specific applications, this article verifies the effectiveness of this technology in detecting the insulation status, mechanical fastening, and internal defects of electrical main equipment. The state detection method for electrical main equipment based on non-contact ultrasonic measurement principle proposed in this article provides a new technical means for the safe and stable operation of electrical equipment, which is helpful for detecting and locating abnormal sound waves in electrified power equipment, and helps on-site maintenance personnel accurately grasp the operating status of electrical equipment.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Fault Diagnosis Based on Image Recognition Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: To efficiently, accurately, and safely test the condition of high-voltage transmission lines, an image recognition method is proposed in this paper. The visible image obtained from aerial photography undergoes preprocessing using the Wiener filter algorithm, followed by feature extraction using the PCA-SIFT algorithm. Subsequently, the image was registered and compared with a reference template image and subjected to change detection technology for fault detection and diagnosis. Testing results demonstrated that the proposed method is capable of fast detecting transmission line faults, which holds significant practical value.

articleTitle: A Reinforcement Learning Compensated Feedback Linearization Controller for Voltage Regulation of Constant Power Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Feedback linearization controllers are widely used for boost converters that regulate the voltage of the power systems integrated by constant power loads (CPL). However, state-of-the-art feedback linearization controllers have two drawbacks. First, feedback linearization controllers are usually designed based on the approximated model of the boost converters, not the detailed model. Second, the feedback linearization controllers are actually model-based. When there are mismatched parameters in the boost converters, the performance of the feedback linearization controller will deteriorate. To handle the model approximation and mismatched parameters, this paper proposes a reinforcement learning compensated feedback linearization (RL-FL) controller. The proposed RL-FL controller utilizes the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) to compensate for the control actions obtained by the feedback linearization (FL) controller to enhance the performance of voltage regulation. Afterwards, a case is studied to verify the enhanced performance of the proposed RL-FL controller compared with the FL controller.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Isolated Three-Port DC-DC Converters Based on Steady-State Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: To assemble various renewable energy sources and the energy storage system, multiport bidirectional DC-DC converters take a significant role in current power system. Four proposed isolated bidirectional three-port DC-DC converters derived from dual-active-bridge (DAB) converter are analysed in this paper. The derivation principles of four proposed topologies are introduced in this paper followed by the steady-state operation analysis. The operation characteristics of the topologies are investigated and illustrated comparatively based on the steady-state operation waveforms, voltage and current characteristic, fault current clear and imbalanced output capability, and the converter worst power rating.

articleTitle: Research on High-Impedance Fault Models Based on Arc Distortion Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The paper addresses the mathematical description problem of nonlinearity and characteristic differentiation in the breakdown of high-impedance fault (HIF) media. It proposes an improved Mayr arc model. Firstly, the physical process of the arc at the fault point and the nonlinear characteristic changes of the arc under high-resistance fault were studied. By analyzing the main characteristic dimensions of the nonlinear resistance, the transferability of model parameters, controllability of nonlinear characteristics, and simulation accuracy were improved. Finally, by comparing the existing high-resistance fault models, the controllability and accuracy of the proposed model were verified. In practice, due to significant differences in fault current waveforms under different grounding media in HIF, traditional detection algorithms often lack adaptability. The improved arc model can accurately depict the arc current waveforms under various working conditions, greatly expanding the applicability of subsequent detection algorithms. This lays a foundation for the accurate detection of HIF.

articleTitle: Adaptive Frequency Modulation Design of BUCK Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Traditional methods for achieving soft switching typically involve adding passive components to the topology, such as in LLC converters. However, these methods can only achieve ZVS (Zero Voltage Switching) turn-on at specific duty cycles and fail to do so across the full duty cycle range. This paper introduces a digital adaptive control method based on a synchronous Buck converter, capable of achieving ZVS turn-on for all switches under any duty cycle condition. To meet the conditions for zero-voltage switching, the method employs a sampling circuit to collect input and output voltages and inductor currents in real time. These values are then used in digital calculations to determine appropriate delay-off times, dead times, and switching frequencies. The soft-switching technology is realized by dynamically adjusting the switching frequency. Finally, simulations and experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed ZVS turn-on scheme across the entire duty cycle range.

articleTitle: Optimized Scheduling of an Integrated Energy System with Multiple Types of Electrolytic Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The hydrogen-containing integrated energy system is an important component of the new power system, and the joint optimization between multiple types of electrolytic cells and randomly fluctuating renewable energy is the key to improving the system performance. In this paper, we propose an optimal scheduling strategy for an electric-hydrogen-thermal coupled integrated energy system considering multiple types of electrolytic cells. The model of alkaline and proton exchange membrane water electrolytic cells is established, and the Gurobi solver is used to solve the comprehensive cost of the system and to minimise the comprehensive cost of the system. The verification of the modified IEEE39-node power system and 6-node thermal system shows that the operation characteristics of different electrolytic cells can further promote the consumption of renewable energy, effectively improve the energy efficiency of the hydrogen production system and reduce the overall cost of the system.

Author Keywords: electrolysis of water for hydrogen production

articleTitle: Synchronization-Based Differential Protection for CT Saturation in Marine Systems with Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In marine electrical systems, differential protection is essential for safeguarding electrical equipment from internal faults. However, current transformer (CT) saturation can cause false operations, especially under high fault currents. This paper introduces a Synchronization-Based Differential Protection (SBDP) method to improve reliability. The method uses the 4–5 millisecond delay before CT saturation, utilizing transient changes in current and voltage as operating signals to ensure fault response while the CT is in its linear region. Upon detecting transient signals, the differential protection relay is opened for 3–4 milliseconds to check for differential signals. If detected, protection is triggered; if not, it is locked to prevent false trips due to CT saturation. Theoretical analysis and practical validation show that this method effectively reduces false operations caused by CT saturation, enhancing the differential protection system's accuracy and reliability. This provides an effective solution for CT saturation in marine electrical systems, ensuring stability under extreme fault conditions.

articleTitle: Distributed Stochastic ACOPF Based on Consensus ADMM and Scenario Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This paper presents a Consensus ADMM-based modeling and solving approach for the stochastic ACOPF. The proposed optimization model considers the load forecasting uncertainty and its induced load-shedding cost via Monte Carlo sampling. The sampled scenarios are reduced using a clustering method combined with simultaneous backward reduction techniques to reduce the computational complexity. The proposed approach is tested on two IEEE systems, achieving about 2% cost reduction and more than 15 times lower reliability index in stochastic load settings compared to the baseline approach.

articleTitle: Efficiency Optimization Method of Parallel DC/DC Converter Based on Sequential Quadratic Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Interleaved parallel bidirectional DC/DC converters are widely used in various application fields due to their high power density and scalability. However, variations in the internal resistance of each module can lead to power switching losses and uneven load current distribution. Consequently, some modules with higher efficiency may operate at non-optimal points, which diminishes the overall system efficiency. Therefore, identifying an optimal load current distribution scheme is crucial. By optimizing the current distribution, each module can operate near its optimal power output point, maximizing overall system efficiency and minimizing energy waste. This paper proposes an efficiency optimization strategy based on the sequential quadratic programming method. By establishing an efficiency model for the parallel DC/DC converter system, we utilize this method to determine the optimal load current distribution. This approach enhances the overall operational efficiency of the system. Simulation results indicate that, compared to traditional current sharing control strategies, the overall system efficiency is improved by up to 1.01%, significantly enhancing energy utilization.

articleTitle: Voltage Drop Compensation Control Method for High-Rate Discharge LBESS Under Variable Frequency Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Lithium battery energy storage system(LBESS) has been widely used in high-power requirement occasions due to its advantages of high specific energy and high specific power. However, under different operating conditions, for high power loads, the output voltage of LBESS will drop due to its own high rate of discharge. For this purpose, a adaptive active disturbance rejection control (A-ADRC) with adaptive adjustment of controller gain is proposed to realize the fast compensation of output voltage under various operating conditions. In addition, the output current of the LBESS generates low-frequency fluctuations due to the influence of the modulation strategy of the secondary inverter and the load imbalance. In order to reduce the output current ripple amplitude of the LBESS, a dynamic notch filter is introduced into the active disturbance rejection controller to suppress the output current ripple under variable frequency conditions. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by Matlab/Simulink simulation.

articleTitle: Research on Testing Methods for Grounding Loop Resistance of High Voltage Cables
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In this paper, a high voltage cable grounding circuit resistance test method is proposed by coupling injection of different frequency signals. Non-power frequency signals are injected into the metal sheath of cross-connected circuit under charged state, and the test voltage, current and voltage current phase difference are extracted. The physical model of cable cross-connected grounding is established, and the measuring device is developed and applied research is carried out. The high voltage cable grounding circuit resistance is accurately measured.

articleTitle: Embedded Machine Learning for Solar PV Power Regulation in a Remote Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This paper presents a machine-learning study for solar inverter power regulation in a remote microgrid. Machine learning models for active and reactive power control are respectively trained using an ensemble learning method. Then, unlike conventional schemes that make inferences on a central server in the far-end control center, the proposed scheme deploys the trained models on an embedded edge-computing device near the inverter to reduce the communication delay. Experiments on a real embedded device achieve matched results as on the desktop PC, with about 0.1ms time cost for each inference input.

articleTitle: The Effect of Epoxy Resin Cracking Under Low Temperature-Stress Coupling Action on its Electrical Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The epoxy coatings of cables in northern regions have been subjected to long-term combined effects of low temperature - stress, resulting in frequent cable failures. To examine the influence of combined low-temperature stress on the electrical characteristics of epoxy resin, this text conducted an aging test of epoxy resin under low-temperature-stress combination, and studied the influence of combined aging on the microstructure and electrical properties of epoxy resin. Furthermore, an electric thermal mechanical multi field coupling model was established to explore the mechanism of the influence of epoxy defects on the insulation of 535kV cable accessories. The results indicate that identical aging duration, as the stress gradually increased from OMPa to 0.3MPa, the cracks of the epoxy resin gradually deepened and widened, and the breakdown voltage gradually decreased, besides, the change in breakdown voltage was particularly significant at a stress of 0.3MPa. Furthermore, the electric field near the epoxy defect of the 535kV cable accessory increased with the increase of the crack.

articleTitle: Improvement of Sensorless Control for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors with Simultaneous Identification of Inductance Based on Pseudo-Random Square Wave Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: As for sensorless control of permanent magnet synchronous motors, various methods based on high-frequency signal injection have been widespread studied. However, with the increasing switching frequency, as well as the injection frequency for better control performance, sharp acoustic noise and electromagnetic interference becomes an issue that cannot be ignored, since the frequency of the signal concentrates on a narrow audible region. Therefore, a novel injection method using high-frequency pseudo-random square wave is proposed in this paper, aiming to effectively decrease high-frequency noises, while maintaining the accuracy and dynamics of sensorless control. Simultaneously, d-axis incremental inductance can be identified in real-time during this process. The corresponding signal demodulation realizes estimation of rotor speed and position by means of a Luenberger observer in stationary reference. Finally, the proposed sensorless control method is verified by simulation. And the power spectra density in fixed frequency and pseudo-random frequency injection schemes are compared.

articleTitle: Mid Term Power Load Forecasting Using Blending Integrated Model Based on Prophet, XGBoost, and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Accurate forecasting of the electrical load provides strong data support for formulating power generation plans. To improve the accuracy of mid-term power load forecasting, this paper combines the power system load data of a certain region's power grid in the past three years to construct three types of power load forecasting models: time series Prophet, deep learning LSTM, and machine learning XGBoost. The goal is to predict the maximum daily load in the region for the next three months. To balance the unique characteristics of each of the three models and their excellent performance in power load forecasting, a blending integrated model based on Prophet, LSTM, and XGBoost was ultimately established for mid-term power load forecasting in the region. The results show that the integrated model has better prediction effect than the single model. Evaluate the accuracy of each model based on four evaluation metrics: MSE, MAE, MAPE, and R-square. The blending ensemble model proposed in this article achieved the best results with all four indicators, with a model accuracy of 97% and an R of 0.93, demonstrating a high degree of model fitting.

articleTitle: Research on the Calibration Method of Battery Internal Resistance Tester
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This paper introduces innovative calibration methods for battery internal resistance testers, specifically targeting the two common calibration methods for such testers-AC injection and AC discharge methods. For the AC injection method, the calibration process and accuracy have been optimized by introducing senseless resistors, coaxial line design, and a high-precision voltage feedback adjustment system, enhancing the accuracy and reliability of the testing process. For the AC discharge method, a constant voltage source in series with a resistor is used to simulate a battery, providing a more convenient and controlled calibration method, while also offering more precise calibration results. The experimental results of this paper demonstrate that the calibration methods proposed can effectively carry out the calibration of battery internal resistance testers, with both AC injection and AC discharge testers achieving resistance and voltage measurement errors within ± 1%. Moreover, the voltage measurement error can be further limited to within 0.5%, showcasing the effectiveness of the new calibration techniques. These findings confirm the significant advantage of the advanced methods in improving calibration precision, providing a reliable technical foundation for assessing battery conditions. This innovation is crucial for ensuring the accuracy of battery internal resistance measurements, which is key to maintaining reliable power systems and optimizing battery performance.

articleTitle: Open-Circuit Fault Diagnosis Method for Interleaved Three-Phase Three-Level DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In this paper, a fault diagnosis method based on output current slope and switch drive signal is proposed for the diagnosis of switch open-circuit fault in interleaved three-phase three-level DC-DC converter. Firstly, the topology of the converter is equivalent through a virtual voltage source, and the inductor current and output current waveforms of the converter under normal operating conditions are analyzed. Secondly, the state of the converter after open-circuit fault is divided into two stages. The circuit state and current time-domain waveform characteristics are analyzed separately. Finally, by combining the drive signal of switch and current waveform characteristics, open-circuit fault diagnosis of the switch is achieved. The simulation results show that proposed fault diagnosis method can effectively detect switch open-circuit fault in interleaved three-phase three-level DC-DC converter.

articleTitle: Eccentricity Error Analysis of Stacked PCB Rogowski Coils
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Rogowski coils based on printed circuit boards (PCBs) are hard coils, having the advantages of uniform conductor distribution, good parameter consistency, and small size compared with traditional Rogowski coils. Restricted by the PCB production process, the Rogowski coil thickness of a single PCB is small, and the sensitivity is low. Moreover, it is impossible to realize dense winding, the measurement results are affected by the position of the conductor to be measured. In order to improve the sensitivity of PCB Rogowski coils, this article proposes a Rogowski coil in which multiple printed circuit boards of the same size are stacked together. Stacking different numbers of PCBs can get different coils heights, improving the sensitivity of PCB Rogowski coils. The eccentricity error calculation model of PCB Rogowski coil with a double half-ring structure in the case of uneven winding and non-coincidence of the centers of the two halves of the ring is established to study the influence of various factors on the measurement eccentricity error of the coil. A low-voltage and variable current experimental platform is built for experimental verification.

articleTitle: Simulation of Performance Optimization of a Latent Heat Thermal Energy Storage Device
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Thermal energy storage (TES) provides a potential adjustable load for the new type of power system. The TES system not only reduces the cost of green power heating, but also realizes thermo-electrolytic coupling, and increases the flexibility of thermal power units. Phase change material (PCM) has been highly concerned in TES system due to the advantages of higher heat storage density and smaller temperature rise during chargedischarge processes. However, the low thermal conductivity of PCM leads to the difficulty in meeting the storage and release efficiency of the TES system for engineering applications. To improve the performance of heat transfer and energy storage of TES system, a two-dimensional computational fluid dynamics model is established and validated. A typical shell and multi-tube energy storage unit was selected to simulate the natural convection, temperature rise and liquid fraction distribution. To optimize thermal storage performance, the eccentricity distance, tube diameter and tube arrangement of the multi-tube energy storage unit were designed using Taguchi orthogonal method. The results show that the total melting time of the original case is 19000 s, of which the melting time of the PCM at the bottom accounts for about 38.4 % of the total time; The optimal case has an eccentricity of 30 mm, a tube diameter of 15 mm and uniform row of tubes. The melting time was 12443 s, which is 52.7 % less than the original case. At 120 min, the average heat storage rate is 882.26 W/m, which is 60 % higher than the original case, and the total heat storage energy reaches a maximum of 10978 kJ/m, which is a significant increase in the heat storage capacity.

articleTitle: Construction of Double Chain Fusion Model of Industrial and Innovation Chain in Power Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This paper analyzes the characteristics of global industrial and supply chains in the post-pandemic era, noting their decentralization, multi-centricity, and localization, alongside heightened concerns about energy security and trade protection. It emphasizes the need to integrate industrial and innovation chains, particularly in the energy sector. Using an evolutionary game model, the study investigates the behaviors and stability of enterprises and academic institutions in both spontaneous and power grid-guided integration paths. Findings suggest that spontaneous integration can lead to stable outcomes of either collaborative innovation or withdrawal, influenced by initial conditions and innovation depth. Conversely, the power grid-guided approach, bolstered by subsidies and support measures, significantly enhances the likelihood of collaboration. Overall, the study concludes that the power grid-guided path is more effective in fostering cooperative innovation between enterprises and academic institutions, providing valuable insights for the energy and power industry's chain integration.

articleTitle: Supply-Demand Balance Optimization Considering Grid-side Energy Storage Station Operation Modes Based on Sequential Production Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The proportion of renewable energy integrated into power systems is continuously increasing on the generation side. The uncertainty and variability in its generation output can potentially cause supply-demand imbalances, leading to power shortages or curtailment of renewable energy at certain times. Grid-side energy storage stations (GESSs) can mitigate generation fluctuations, and provide regulation capacities during supply-demand mismatches, playing a critical role in the supply-demand balance of the system. This paper proposes a supply-demand balance optimization model considering GESS operation modes. The charging/discharging power of GESSs is modeled using discrete power levels, and constraints are introduced to ensure the operational profitability of GESSs. This model can simulate single-cycle or double-cycle operation modes of GESSs under the peak-valley pricing policy, providing balance solutions that reflect the actual system operating environment. Finally, the proposed model is verified on an inter-provincial case system, demonstrating the model's analytical capabilities and simulation effectiveness using real data.

articleTitle: Calculation and Improvement Method of Inter-Regional Available Transmission Capacity for Power Systems Including Wind Power
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The management of power system transmission congestion becomes more complex due to the randomness of wind power. Therefore, it is necessary to propose a method for calculating the available transmission capability (ATC) of power systems that include wind power and seek measures from the load side to alleviate transmission congestion. Firstly, we analyze the calculation principle of the power transfer distribution factor (PTDF) and the load demand response (DR) rule based on maximizing net benefits to customers. Then, we derive a calculation method for inter-regional ATC based on PTDF and design a process for finding the optimal implementation location of DR to solve transmission congestion. Using an improved IEEE-30 system as a basis, we calculate inter-regional ATC values, identify optimal locations for implementing DR in different scenarios, and compare and analyze inter-regional ATC values before and after implementing DR. The results demonstrate that our proposed method effectively solves related problems.

articleTitle: Configuration Optimization of Dispatchable Sources of Large Clean Energy Base
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The northwest region of China possesses abundant renewable energy resources. Due to low regional electricity demand and the significant distance from load center, the area faces challenges if positioned as a power export system. These challenges, which include weak regional grid structure and limited number of supportive power sources, make it difficult to meet the energy supply requirements from the receiving end. A time-sequence simulation model of a large-scale clean energy base in a specific northwest region of China is established in this paper. The optimization of dispatchable sources configuration is carried out by considering various constraints such as the utilization rate of renewable energy, the penetration of renewable energy, and the power production confidence rate. The findings provide valuable insights for formulating strategies for the delivery and consumption of renewable energy from the northwest region.

articleTitle: Low-Carbon Economic Dispatch of an Integrated Agricultural Energy System Considering Biomass Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In the context of the “carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals” goals, to improve the energy utilization efficiency of the integrated agricultural energy system (IAES), mitigate the impact of IAES on the weak rural distribution network, enhance the system's ability to accommodate wind power, and further improve the carbon reduction capability of IAES, this paper proposes a low-carbon economic dispatch strategy for IAES. Firstly, it considers using crop straw as fuel for biomass power generation, participating in intraday dispatch to enhance source-side flexibility. It further explores the carbon reduction potential of IAES through the negative carbon emission effect of biomass energy carbon capture and storage (BECCS) combined with a tiered carbon trading mechanism. Finally, through adjustable combined heat and power (CHP) units, low-temperature waste heat power generation devices based on the organic Rankine cycle (ORC), and air source heat pumps, the original problem is formulated as a mixed-integer linear problem with the objective of minimizing energy purchase costs and carbon emission costs. The CPLEX commercial solver is used to solve the problem, and the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is validated through comparisons across multiple scenarios.

articleTitle: Strategy of Technological Development of State Grid Based on the SWOT-PEST Matrix Model
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In recent years, the global energy transition has entered a phase of accelerated advancement, and China has also stepped into a new stage of building a modern energy system. How to break through core key technologies, strategically position cutting-edge technologies, and promote the digital transformation of the power system has become a pressing issue for the State Grid Corporation of China. Based on the SWOT-PEST matrix model, this paper systematically analyzes the opportunities and threats from the external macro-environment, including political, economic, social, and technological aspects, as well as the internal micro strengths and weaknesses in the technological development of the State Grid Corporation. It proposes specific strategies for future technological development, management innovation, and market expansion, providing strategic guidance for the company's new round of energy transition in the medium and long term.

articleTitle: Robust Optimal Scheduling Method of Electric-Gas-Traffic Network Coupling System Based on Traffic Flow Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The volatility of traffic flow in the operation of new energy vehicles creates an imbalance between energy supply and demand. By taking into account the temporal aspect of traffic network functioning and the cost associated with energy consumption in the electric-gas coupling network, the objective is to minimize the cost of operating the day ahead. The data-driven algorithm and risk coefficient method are combined to describe the situation. The fuzzy uncertainty set of traffic flow is generated, and a three-layer robust optimal scheduling model is constructed taking into account the uncertainty of traffic flow. The approach involves integrating the optimality condition (Karush-Kuhn-Tucker, KKT) with the column-and-constraints generation technique. The efficacy of the proposed framework and solution approach is ultimately confirmed by a numerical illustration, demonstrating that the suggested strategy may proficiently address the energy demand uncertainty associated with new energy vehicle and achieve positive interaction between the network and the higher network.

articleTitle: A Real Time Frequency Response Control Strategy Design Method for Virtual Control Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: By utilizing virtual power plant technology, a vast array of distributed energy resources on the distribution side can be aggregated into virtual control units (VCU), allowing them to function as independent entities that can be directly regulated by the grid control center to participate in frequency response control. This approach helps alleviate the shortage of frequency response resources caused by the withdrawal of conventional units due to the large-scale integration of renewable energy sources. However, there has been limited research on the implementation models and control strategies for frequency response control of distributed energy resources (DER). This paper investigates the real-time control modes and control strategies for distributed energy resources within virtual control units. Based on the analysis of factors influencing the operational states of three types of distributed energy resources-electric vehicles, energy storage, and demand response-we identify concise and efficient reporting information that reflects their operational status. By integrating existing regulation processes with the response characteristics of distributed energy resources, we select suitable rolling control modes and time scales, thereby designing a control mode and workflow characterized by “online budgeting and real-time control.” Using the reporting information and control mode as a foundation, we establish a real-time control model for distributed energy resources. Simulation results demonstrate that the constructed model can optimize the allocation of distributed energy resources, maximizing the benefits of the virtual control unit while fulfilling the assigned control responsibilities.

articleTitle: Evolved Gambling Analysis of Power Industry Innovation Alliance Under the Chain Leader System
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This paper discusses the challenges our country faces in key areas of core technology, where we remain dependent on others, with high-end manufacturing equipment reliant on imports, and bottlenecks in critical links of the industrial chain. The focus is on the unique advantages of the State Grid Corporation of China as the leader of the industrial chain and its pivotal role in fostering collaborative innovation across the chain. Using evolutionary game theory, a three-party model is established involving the “chain leader,” “chain master,” and other members, to analyze the behavior and evolutionary stability strategies of each player. The study also explores the key factors influencing the modern power system's industrial chain. Results indicate that factors such as the subsidy intensity provided by the chain leader, regulatory costs, and the reward-punishment mechanisms significantly affect the high-quality development of the industrial alliance. Finally, the paper outlines the State Grid's path to fulfilling its role as chain leader through three mechanisms: leadership, research-engineering integration, and industry-university-research-application coordination.

articleTitle: A Precision-Compensated Linear Power Flow Model Based on Mapping Voltage Magnitudes from Logarithmic Space to Squared Space
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Linear power flow is widely applied in various areas of power systems. The DC power flow model is a classical linear power flow model, but its main limitation is the inability to account for voltage magnitude. Other classical models that consider voltage magnitude are typically linearized in the original voltage magnitude space, leading to a computational accuracy bottleneck. To address this issue, this study first proposes an improved linear power flow model. The model remaps the voltage magnitude from logarithmic space to square space, preserving the nonlinear characteristics of the original current equation and compensating for the voltage phase angle. This approach overcomes the accuracy bottleneck of classical models. Then, through matrix partitioning and transformation, the model achieves complete decoupling of the voltage magnitude and phase angle, avoiding nonconvex quadratic programming problems in optimization and enhancing computational efficiency. Finally, the accuracy and speed of the proposed model are validated through simulations across multiple test systems.

articleTitle: Intra-Day Rolling Optimal Strategy Considering Whole Dispatch Process and Multi-Type Adjustable Measures
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The current electric power system practices hierarchical and zonal administration to facilitate more effective monitoring of grid safety and event management. With an escalating integration of new energy sources on the generation side, the intrinsically variable nature of these resources introduces substantial uncertainties into grid operations. Meanwhile, on the demand side, load profiles are diversifying further, significantly influenced by weather conditions, market price signals, or incentive schemes, thereby adding another layer of unpredictability. Against this context, this paper proposes an intra-day rolling optimal strategy considering whole dispatch process and multi-type adjustable measures. By synthesizing regulating resources from both the source and load sides, it undertakes a series of intra-day rolling optimization decisions across the entire dispatch workflow. This strategy aims to harmonize and optimize the allocation of various resources, thereby ensuring the secure and stable functioning of the electrical grid amidst the complexities introduced by the integration of intermittent renewables and the dynamics of diversified loads.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Research on the Output and Economic Sensitivity of the Integrated System of Photovoltaic and Energy Storage Under the Load Demand Orientation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Household energy storage has significant capabilities to optimize the user load curve and assist in coordinating distributed photovoltaic power generation. In order to explore the output of the integrated photovoltaic and energy storage and its economic sensitivity more deeply, this article builds an integrated photovoltaic and energy storage operation model based on the load demand, and takes a certain household energy storage in Xi'an as an example to conduct in-depth analysis of the integrated photovoltaic and energy storage system through software simulation. The research shows that configuring energy storage can greatly reduce the amplitude of load fluctuations, make the photovoltaic output more stable, significantly improve the self-consumption rate of photovoltaic, and reduce the amount of electricity bills paid by users actually. For example, in this case, the study found that after configuring energy storage, the self-consumption rate of photovoltaic power can be increased by 36.92%, and the user's electricity bill can be reduced by 45,631 yuan. Moreover, when the self-consumption rate of the photovoltaic power generation system is at a relatively high level, the financial sensitivity coefficient of the energy storage cost and the grid-connected electricity price is relatively high, and it should be set as the main control item, while the electricity purchase price is set as the secondary control item, so as to effectively enhance the financial risk resistance ability of the engineering project. The results of this study are of great significance for promoting the development process of the integrated household photovoltaic and energy storage.

Author Keywords: Regarding integrated photovoltaic and energy storage

articleTitle: The Optimal Pricing Strategy for Travel Cost Budget Electric-Transportation Coupling Network is Considered
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: With the large-scale development of electric vehicles, it is of great significance to study how to effectively consider the user's travel behavior mechanism and formulate a reasonable grid charging price for the collaborative optimization scheduling of electric transportation network. Aiming at this problem, this paper proposes a charging station pricing strategy considering user's travel cost budget in electric-transportation coupling network. Firstly, a transportation user's equilibrium model considering travel cost budget was established, and variational inequality was used to equivalently describe the equilibrium state, so as to describe the travel demand and charging behavior of electric vehicles.
