Secondly, a second-order cone optimization model of distribution network considering power reduction was constructed, and the charging station pricing problem was transformed into an optimization problem with variational inequality constraints. To solve this problem, an alternating iterative algorithm and an outer gradient algorithm are designed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed model and method is verified by an example, and the results show the necessity of considering travel cost budget in coupled network pricing.

articleTitle: Stability Region Analysis of the GFL-GFM System Based on Impedance Method
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of power electronic converters, maintaining power system stability has become significantly challenging. Nowadays, extensive stability analyses have focused on the interactions between converters and the grid, as well as between multiple converters, which often overlook the impact of different operating points on stability. This paper investigates the stability of a typical system combining a Grid-Following inverter (GFL) with a Grid-Forming inverter (GFM) under various operating conditions. Firstly, impedance-based methods for stability analysis are developed, and the procedure for determining stability regions is outlined. Then, it compares the stability regions across various GFM capacity configurations and assesses the impact of different system operating points on stability. Finally, the proposed methods are employed to delineate the system's stability region, and the accuracy of the analysis and the stability region is validated using a time-domain model implemented in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Construction and Implementation of “Model Room for Ultra High Voltage Important Transmission Channels” Based on Digital Control
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: With the increasingly complex operation environment of UHV transmission line channels, and in order to meet the requirements of the construction and development of new power systems and digital and intelligent power grids, State Grid Shanxi UHV Transmission Company has built and implemented a “model room for important UHV transmission channels” based on digital and intelligent control. Firstly, a full-view collaborative three-dimensional inspection system was constructed through technologies such as unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) autonomous inspection and channel visualization. Secondly, improve the transmission panoramic IoT monitoring platform to realize realtime monitoring and intelligent early warning of transmission equipment and channels; Finally, a differentiated management and control system for power grid risk should be established to improve the refinement and efficiency of power grid risk management through accurate assessment and control measures. The implementation results show that the model room has significantly improved the digital intelligence level and management quality and efficiency of transmission operation and maintenance, enhanced the power supply reliability of UHV transmission channels, and achieved significant economic and social benefits. This study provides a practical case and reference for the development of digital intelligence in power grids, and is of great significance for promoting the sustainable and healthy development of UHV power grid construction.

articleTitle: Two-Timescale Rolling Dispatch of RCs and MESSs During Distribution System Restoration
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: To repair distribution networks damaged by hurricanes, mobile energy storage systems (MESSs), wind energy, and repair collaborates (RCs) are typically arranged. But still, hurricanes can continue to cause damage during restoration, leading to new faults and interruptions in wind power. To address these issues, this paper introduces a two-stage rolling dispatch method across two timescales, taking into account the different response speeds of vehicle scheduling and system operations. Over an extended period, the scheduling of MESSs and RCs vehicles is optimized by the use of rolling optimization framework in the first-stage model to handle following faults, and projected wind speeds and load needs. Distributed generators (DGs) and MESS output decisions are made with real-time value on a short timescale. To make solving the nonlinear wind power cut-off model easier, it is also converted into a mixed-integer linear programming form. The approach is validated using the modified IEEE-69 distribution network. Results show that this approach effectively coordinates resources, reduces load loss, and improves system resilience to wind power cut-offs and faults during hurricanes.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Location in DC Distribution Network Based on Hybrid Whale Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Aiming at the current DC distribution network fault model complexity, lower fault location accuracy, slower convergence speed and greater influence by the transition resistance and other problems, this paper adopts the hybrid whale algorithm to improve and solve the problem. First of all, this paper establishes the mathematical models of inter-pole faults and single-pole grounding faults on the basis of the six-terminal ring DC distribution network model, introduces the local search mechanism of bat algorithm on the basis of whale optimization algorithm, forms the hybrid whale algorithm, formulates the fault localization principle based on the hybrid whale algorithm, and introduces the data culling and data completion methods based on the local outlier factor method and moving average method. Through experimental simulation, the fault localization method is verified to have the advantages of high localization accuracy and small influence by transition resistance, and the localization error under data distortion is reduced through data processing. Finally, the hybrid whale algorithm is compared with other intelligent algorithms to verify that the hybrid whale algorithm has the advantages of high accuracy and fast convergence speed.

articleTitle: Transient Modeling and Dynamic Response Characteristics Analysis of Doubly-Fed Variable Speed Pumped Storage Unit Under Pumping Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In contrast to traditional fixed-speed pumped storage unit, doubly-fed variable-speed pumped storage unit (DFVSPSU) offer a spacious range of power regulation and higher working effectiveness. However, due to the diverse operating conditions and intricate mode transitions associated with DFVSPSU, a comprehensive analysis of their mode transition characteristics is essential. Firstly, we develop a mathematical model for the DFVSPUS under pumping conditions, incorporating the dynamic behavior of the fluid within the water conduit as well as the added frictional effects from the guide vane. Subsequently, a simulation model of the unit was built in Simulink, using both pumping and shutdown conditions as case studies, and validated the model through simulation. Finally, the results demonstrate that the model effectively manages the transition of operating conditions. When the active power reference value changes, the unit's power, speed, and guide vane opening accurately follow the reference or optimal values, confirming the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed model, and the established model is validated through simulation.

articleTitle: The Impact of Gate Resistance of IGBT and SiC MOSFET on the Dynamic Parameters of Si/SiC Hybrid Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) and the silicon carbide metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (SiC MOSFET) hybrid devices combine the high current-handling capability of IGBTs with the superior high-frequency performance and efficiency of SiC MOSFETs, providing a balanced trade-off between cost and performance compared to fully SiC-based solutions. The gate drive resistances of both the IGBT and the SiC MOSFET play a crucial role in determining their switching speeds and sequences, which in turn impact the overall switching characteristics of the hybrid device. In this paper, a double-pulse simulation circuit for Si/SiC hybrid devices is constructed to investigate the effects of varying gate resistances of the IGBT and SiC MOSFET on the device's switching behavior, and the corresponding influence mechanism is analysed. The findings indicate that by adjusting the gate resistances of the IGBT and SiC MOSFET, it is possible to modify the relative initial switching times and sequences of the devices, thereby affecting key dynamic parameters such as voltage and current overshoot, as well as switching losses. This study provides valuable insights into optimizing the performance of Si/SiC hybrid devices by reducing the risk of dynamic overvoltage and overcurrent, as well as minimizing switching losses. However, further investigations are required to establish an efficient method for selecting appropriate gate resistances.

articleTitle: Novel Frequency Control Strategy for Photovoltaic Storage Power Stations in Electric Power Systems Based on Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This paper proposes a new frequency regulation control strategy for photovoltaic and energy storage stations within new power systems based on Model Predictive Control (MPC). This control strategy aims to minimize the sum of system frequency deviation and the rate of change of frequency and optimizes the active power output of the stations and participates in system frequency regulation through the control of their active output. Finally, simulation examples demonstrate that the proposed method offers superior frequency regulation and quickly and precisely determine the output of photovoltaic and energy storage stations under multiple constraints, thus enhancing the system's frequency stability.

articleTitle: Optimization Configuration of Agricultural Comprehensive Energy System Considering Generalized Comprehensive Demand Response and System Flexibility
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: To further tap into the potential of the user side, improve the economic efficiency of the integrated energy system, and achieve source load friendly interaction, a dual layer optimization configuration model for the integrated energy system considering generalized comprehensive demand response is proposed. Firstly, the generalized comprehensive demand response mechanism is introduced in the upper layer model, and the loads participating in the demand response are divided into three categories: transferable, reducible, and replaceable, so that they can participate in the system operation. The improved particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to solve the problem with the total system cost as the objective function. The optimal scheduling result is simulated in the lower layer model, and the mixed integer linear programming method is used to solve the problem with the system operation cost as the objective function. Finally, the optimized configuration result and corresponding optimized operation plan are obtained. Finally, the model was validated through case analysis to reduce system configuration and operating costs, minimize peak valley differences of various loads, and alleviate energy supply pressure.

articleTitle: Design of Cloud-Based Smart Meters and Optimization of Information and Energy Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The integration of smart grid technologies offers transformative opportunities for power system upgrades by merging traditional power infrastructures with advanced energy, information, and communication technologies. This integration aims to achieve efficient power distribution and optimized utilization. However, challenges such as maintaining power supply-demand equilibrium, ensuring grid security, and improving data processing efficiency persist. To address these issues, this paper proposes an innovative cloud-based smart grid architecture. The proposed architecture stratifies the grid into three layers: the cloud layer, the intermediate layer, and the user layer, facilitating efficient interaction and management of both information flow and energy flow. By employing this architecture, the paper develops a smart system capable of effectively processing multi-source heterogeneous data, optimizing supply-demand balance, and enhancing grid security. This approach significantly improves the efficiency and accuracy of power data processing, fortifies system security and stability, and establishes a robust technical foundation for the future advancement of smart grids.

articleTitle: Research on Real-Time Temperature Monitoring System for Dry-Type Transformers Based on Optical Fiber Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Transformer overheating is a critical factor affecting the reliability of power systems. Traditional temperature control strategies either fail to closely track load variations or struggle to achieve comprehensive internal temperature monitoring of the transformer. To address this issue, this paper constructs a transformer fiber optic temperature measurement system, achieving three-dimensional visualized real-time monitoring of the surface temperature of core components. Firstly, this paper designs a multimode fiber routing scheme and determines the installation positions for fiber Bragg grating sensors. Subsequently, loss testing and compensation were conducted to ensure the accuracy of the measurement results. A temperature rise experiment was then performed, and the results were compared with thermal imaging to verify the accuracy of the temperature monitoring system. Based on the experimental data, the changes in hotspot positions and temperature rise patterns of various core components were analyzed. Finally, the developed algorithms for loss calibration, noise reduction processing, and visualization were integrated into software, realizing three-dimensional visualized real-time monitoring of the surface temperature distribution of the transformer. This provides a solution for the digital twin of the transformer.

articleTitle: A Distributed Optimization Algorithm Considering Inequality Constraints and its Application in Economic Dispatch Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The economic dispatch problem (EDP) is crucial in optimizing and controlling power systems. As modern power system become more complex, traditional centralized communication methods are becoming less reliable. Therefore, distributed optimization method that relie on communication between neighboring nodes without the need for a central node are proposed. Existing distributed optimization methods for economic dispatch problems mainly focus on equality constraints like supply-demand balance, while problems with global inequality constraints are rarely studied. To address this gap, we propose a distributed optimization algorithm based on the primal-dual method and gradient tracking technique that can handle both global equality and inequality constraints. We thoroughly analyze its convergence and successfully apply it to the EDP with emission constraints to demonstrate its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Power Prediction Based on the Error Probability Distribution Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Accurate prediction of PV output is of great significance to the operation and scheduling of power system. In order to improve the prediction accuracy of photovoltaic power generation, this paper proposes to first fit the distribution law of the preliminary prediction error of photovoltaic power based on the Gauss mixed model (GMM), and then compensate the predicted value of the error to the original point prediction result to achieve the photovoltaic output prediction. A PV point prediction model based on long short-term memory network (LSTM) is constructed in the first place. Due to environmental factors such as light intensity, temperature and visibility, the prediction results of PV power generation output will be greatly affected. By using K-means clustering algorithm (K-means), the historical PV output data is divided into multiple weather scenarios, and then the distribution probability of error between the predicted value and the actual value is modeled and analyzed in different weather scenarios. Through the model fitting results under the specified confidence level interval, the predicted value of PV power point is modified and the final prediction interval is obtained. Finally, the fitting results of Gaussian mixture distribution are compared with those of normal distribution, t distribution and logistic distribution model. The results show that the probability distribution model is more accurate and reliable than the traditional distribution model.
